footnotes: From pre-tax loss to net loss to Jackson Financial: includes an $186M income tax benefit; after $45.0M attributable to noncontrolling interests, $44.0M of preferred dividends. The income statement has no operating income line; it is shown here as revenue less the operating expense lines, with interest and other non-operating items below it. The filing reports no separate capital expenditures, so free cash flow equals operating cash flow.

Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC (income statement lines as the filing presents them); free cash flow = operating cash flow − capital expenditures. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue rose 2.0× to $6.7B in 2025. Operating income fell 45.9% to $1.2B, a 18.1% margin.

The company had a net loss of $17.0M, or −$0.24 per share, versus net income of $902M. Operating cash flow was $5.8B and free cash flow $5.8B, versus $5.8B; Jackson Financial returned $892M through dividends and buybacks.
watch: Net income includes a $186M tax benefit.
sources: Jackson Financial Inc. Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)
